prompt: Match each part of a rota to what it is.

pairs.right: paged when the first page goes unacknowledged
midweek, so no shift starts on a Monday

right_distractors: the person who fixes everything alone

prompt: A rota of five people, one week each. What share of their weeks is each person on call, in percent?
Why does the lesson say a team of five carries a pager with no margin?

choices.text: Because five people cannot cover nights
choices.why: They can; the problem is absences.

choices.text: One holiday makes it one week in four
choices.why: Right. Two absences make it one in three.

choices.text: Because the SRE book forbids teams of five
choices.why: It recommends about eight for full coverage; it forbids nothing.

choices.text: Because the tech lead is not paid for it
choices.why: Pay is not the reason given.

prompt: A page arrives and the problem is bigger than one person. What is the person on call's job?

choices.text: To fix it alone before anybody else wakes
choices.why: The rota is not a promise to fix everything alone.

choices.text: To wait until morning and report it
choices.why: A page is answered within minutes.

choices.text: To find out whose change caused it
choices.why: That is blame, and it is not the job.

choices.text: To acknowledge, assess and call for help
choices.why: Right. Often by declaring an incident.

prompt: Put the Billing team's escalation, when nobody acknowledges, in order.
What is the difference between the two directions of escalation?

choices.text: Up when nobody answers; across to who knows
choices.why: Right. The first is mechanical, the second a judgement.

choices.text: Up is for nights, across is for days
choices.why: Time of day is not what separates them.

choices.text: Up goes to managers, across to customers
choices.why: Neither goes to customers.

choices.text: There is no difference; both are automatic
choices.why: Only the first is done by the tool.

prompt: Rafa was paged 54 times, and 29 of those came from other people's weeks. How many came in his own weeks on call?
Which costs of always passing card problems to Rafa does the lesson name? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: Rafa never has a week off the pager
choices.why: An expert reachable every week is on call every week.

choices.text: The others do not learn the card code
choices.why: Every problem passed on is one they did not solve.

choices.text: The team has a single point of failure
choices.why: The night Rafa is away, nobody knows the code.

choices.text: Incidents take longer to resolve
choices.why: Passing to the expert usually shortens an incident; the cost is elsewhere.

prompt: Which change spreads Rafa's knowledge without making incidents longer?

choices.text: Forbid passing pages to Rafa
choices.why: That would only make incidents longer.

choices.text: Take Rafa off the rota entirely
choices.why: The knowledge leaves with him.

choices.text: Rafa joins a call; the on-call types
choices.why: Right. The person on call learns the commands.

choices.text: Page Rafa first for everything
choices.why: That makes the problem the rule.

prompt: Under which heading of the handover note does "month-end today" belong?

choices.text: open
choices.why: Open is for unresolved incidents and promises.

choices.text: coming
choices.why: Right. What the next week holds that could break things.

choices.text: noise
choices.why: Noise is for alerts that needed nobody.

choices.text: changed
choices.why: Changed is for releases still settling.

prompt: What does the fifteen-minute call add to the written note?

choices.text: A signature from the tech lead
choices.why: Nobody signs a handover.

choices.text: A copy for the managers
choices.why: The note is for the person starting.

choices.text: A count of the pages
choices.why: The note already lists them.

choices.text: The questions the note did not answer
choices.why: Right. It is where the missing sentence comes out.

prompt: Why does the lesson call the "pages this week" heading a measurement?

choices.text: It records whether each page needed a person
choices.why: Right. Kept over weeks, it says which alerts are worth waking for.

choices.text: Because it is copied into the error budget
choices.why: The budget counts bad events, not pages.

choices.text: Because managers grade the person on call by it
choices.why: It is not a grade for people.

choices.text: Because the paging tool requires it
choices.why: No tool requires it.

prompt: When a shift ends during an incident, the outgoing person stays until the incoming one says out loud that they ___ it.
Which form of compensation does the lesson say costs least and is most often forgotten?

choices.text: A fixed amount per week on call
choices.why: That is one of the three, not the one forgotten.

choices.text: Payment for hours actually worked
choices.why: That is one of the three, not the one forgotten.

choices.text: Time off after a night page
choices.why: Right. A late start after a bad night.

choices.text: A bonus at the end of the year
choices.why: Not one of the forms the lesson names.

prompt: Under CLT art. 244, §2, an hour of sobreaviso counts at what fraction of the normal hourly wage? Give it as a percentage, to the nearest whole number.
According to Súmula 428 of the TST, does carrying a company phone make an employee on sobreaviso?

choices.text: Yes, whenever the phone is switched on
choices.why: The phone alone is not enough.

choices.text: Not alone; only on a duty schedule
choices.why: Right. Controlled at a distance, callable during rest.

choices.text: No, sobreaviso only applies to railway workers
choices.why: Courts apply it by analogy to other workers.

choices.text: Only if the employee works at night
choices.why: Night work is not the test.

prompt: A rota pages every night, and the team is paid well for it. What does the lesson say about that?

choices.text: It is a price for burning people out
choices.why: Right. Pay makes on-call fair; fixing alerts makes it bearable.

choices.text: It is fair, so nothing else is needed
choices.why: Fair is not the same as bearable.

choices.text: The pay should be cut to force fixes
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson suggests cutting pay.

choices.text: It is illegal in Brazil
choices.why: The lesson makes no such claim.

prompt: The SRE book's ceiling is two incidents per twelve-hour shift. How many is that in a week of round-the-clock shifts?
The Billing team's totals were well under the ceiling. What was the problem?

choices.text: There were too many pages overall
choices.why: About six a week is far under the ceiling.

choices.text: Nobody answered at night
choices.why: Night pages were answered.

choices.text: The paging tool lost pages
choices.why: Nothing says pages were lost.

choices.text: Where the pages landed
choices.why: Right. Rafa took 54 and Caio 6.

prompt: Why does the Billing team give the month-end its own secondary?

choices.text: Because the provider asked for it
choices.why: The provider has no say in the rota.

choices.text: So that Rafa can rest at month-end
choices.why: It is about everybody, not Rafa alone.

choices.text: So the calendar does not pick who gets it
choices.why: Right. It had picked the same people for three months.

choices.text: Because month-end needs a manager
choices.why: The second person is chosen in turn.

prompt: With Bia joining, the rota has six people. What share of weeks is each person on call, to the nearest whole percent?
Why is on-call load measured per person rather than for the team?

choices.text: Because team totals are hard to compute
choices.why: They are easy; they hide the problem.

choices.text: Averages hide one person carrying half
choices.why: Right. The team-wide numbers looked healthy.

choices.text: To rank people by how often they are paged
choices.why: It is about the load, not a ranking.

choices.text: Because the law requires it
choices.why: The lesson's reason is not legal.

prompt: Which signal does the lesson give that a rota is failing before anybody says so?

choices.text: People swap weeks away and stop volunteering
choices.why: Right. The failure is quiet.

choices.text: The paging tool sends a warning
choices.why: No tool measures willingness.

choices.text: The error budget runs out
choices.why: That is about the service, not the people.

choices.text: The SLA is broken
choices.why: A contract with customers says nothing about the rota.

prompt: Every page wakes the person on call, and 29 of 82 also woke Rafa. How many times in all did a page wake somebody?
